data.name: Jakub
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Yaakov', meaning 'he who supplants'. In the Bible, Jacob is a deceiver, who tricks his father into blessing him instead of his older brother, Esau. Despite his deceitful actions, God blesses him and renames him 'Israel' – 'he who struggles with God'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reminding us of God's mercy and the power of perseverance.

in_hebrew.name: יעקב
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא יחליף, יעקב הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'הוא יחליף'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יעקב הוא שם עברי שמקורו מהמילה 'עקב', שפירושו 'עקב' או 'קשור'. השם יעקב מוזכר במקרא כבן של יצחק ואביו של יוסף ויהודה. השם יעקב הוא אחד השמות הנפוצים ביותר בתנ'ך ויש לו חשיבות רבה במסורת היהודית והנוצרית. השם יעקב מסמל את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים ואת היכולת להתגבר על הקשיים.

in_greek.name: Ιακώβ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιακώβ είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יעקב (יעקב). Στο Χριστιανισμό, ο Ιακώβ αναφέρεται συχνά στον Ιακώβ, τον αδελφό του Κυρίου, ο οποίος ήταν ένας από τους πρώτους ηγετών της Εκκλησίας στην Ιερουσαλήμ. Ο Ιακώβ είναι σημαντικός και στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη, όπου αναφέρεται ως ο πατέρας των Ιουδαίων και ο γιος του Ισαάκ.

in_latin.name: Iacobus
in_latin.meaning: Supplanter, Iacobus means 'supplanter' or 'he who replaces'
in_latin.long_meaning: Iacobus is the Latin form of the Hebrew name יעקב (Iacob). In Christian tradition, Iacobus is associated with Saint James, the brother of Jesus and one of the leaders of the early Christian Church in Jerusalem. The name Iacobus symbolizes the idea of supplanting or replacing, reflecting the biblical story of Jacob and Esau.

in_english.name: Jakub
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jakub originates from the Hebrew name יעקב (Iacob), meaning 'he who replaces' or 'supplanter'. In Christian tradition, Jakub is associated with Saint James, the brother of Jesus. The name has been adopted into various cultures, including Polish, Czech, and Slovak, and remains a popular name in many Christian communities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jakub has a rich cultural heritage in the Christian faith, as it is the name of one of the twelve apostles, known as Saint James the Greater. He is the son of Zebedee and the brother of John the Beloved. Jakub plays an important role in the early Christian community, and his name became a common one in Christian communities throughout history. In some countries, such as Poland, the name Jakub is the most popular given Christian name.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name Jakub carries the message of struggle, perseverance, and ultimately, God's grace and redemption. Just like the biblical Jacob, who deceitfully obtained the blessing, but later in life, wrestled with God and received a new name and a blessing, the name Jakub invites us to reflect on our own spiritual journeys. It reminds us that even if we have made mistakes or gone astray, God is always ready to forgive, redeem, and bless us. The name Jakub is a powerful reminder of God's mercy and grace, and the importance of persevering in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Jacob was the third son and second survivor of the twelve sons of Isaac and Rebekah. The name Jakub carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
